title: ICP · hotel operators
summary: Hotel operators are two marketed subsegments—independent hotels and hotel groups—defined by guest communication, property or group knowledge, and PMS context, not a generic hospitality label. Public proof in this pack is one boutique owner-operator story; group-scale outcomes and operations-led purchases remain investigate-not-reject gaps.
markdown:
Treat hotel operators as two site industries—**Independent Hotels** and **Hotel Groups**—not one vague hospitality ICP. Short-term rentals are a separate segment; use [ICP · vacation-rental operators](#knowledge/icp-rentals) and do not import STR automation rates as hotel proof. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)

FAQs state Conduit is for hotel teams, serviced-apartment operators, and short-term rental managers, with agents answering guest messages and calls, handling routine requests, and coordinating with the team. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

## Account definition

**Independent hotels** are marketed as property-level guest operations: agents answer calls and messages while the team looks after people at the desk, using that hotel’s policies and booking details, including after hours. The buying locus in the copy is the desk—front office, reservations, overnight cover—not a corporate shared-services org. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)

**Hotel groups** are marketed as a portfolio workspace: handle messages and calls across the group, share brand standards, and still give agents each property’s policies and reservation details (parent + child listings, shared knowledge base, org structure). Calls are described as landing in a shared inbox. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups)

A site claim of being trusted by 300+ hospitality brands in 120+ countries is company reach language, not named hotel-group adoption. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups)

The only named **hotel** customer body in this pack is The Lauderdale Boutique Hotel (using Conduit since December 2024; founder Noel Poler). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel)

## Best-fit operating situations

Fit is a communication-and-action job around the stay, not “unattended hotel.” Product pages describe answering across voice, chat, email, WhatsApp, and connected OTA threads; acting through supported tools; escalating with history. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

| Operating load | Independent Hotels page | Hotel Groups page | Surface |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Night / late arrival / in-stay | After-hours receptionist; overnight cover; late check-in | Voice + omnichannel; calls in shared inbox | [AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents) |
| Desk volume and handoffs | Always-on front desk | Omnichannel inbox; multi-property conversations | [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox) |
| Extras during the stay | Room upgrades, spa, dining | Loyalty/perks, upgrades, spa and dining | [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows), [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals) |
| Consistency | One hotel’s brand voice | Shared brand voice plus property knowledge | Inbox views by property or team |

Lauderdale’s attributed pattern is an owner replacing inconsistent call-center models (costs cited from $4,000 down to $1,200, then Conduit at $600/month) with an “AI-powered support platform and 24/7 staffed support team,” faster replies, fewer refunds, and NOI/cap-rate math. That is one boutique, hands-off-investment story—not a typical hotel outcome. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel)

**Scenario A — good-fit (hypothetical, unlabeled property):** A single independent hotel whose night team still takes late-arrival calls and WhatsApp, with Opera or Mews already in use, and a GM willing to maintain property policies. The job is coverage plus reservation context, not removing the desk.

**Scenario B — uncertain (hypothetical):** A group whose RFP is enterprise CRM, labor/payroll, or portfolio housekeeping as the must-have. Group use-case pages describe those themes, while the product nav labels Operations coming soon. Investigate whether live need is guest communication. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents)

**Scenario C — poor-fit (hypothetical):** A buyer who needs a physical self-check-in kiosk. Group copy: Conduit supports guest communication; it is not a physical check-in kiosk. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups)

## Company and technology profile

No public room-count, flag, or chain-scale cutoff. Commercial packaging is per unit per month with starting rates, scaling beyond 50 listings; 0–25 units has a Startup full-feature monthly price. Map packages in a sales conversation rather than treating a bundle rate as an Agents-only price. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

Hotel industry pages name Opera, Mews, Cloudbeds, Apaleo, RMS Cloud, StayNTouch, Booking.com, Expedia, WhatsApp, and email; the hotel-groups stack card also lists Salesforce. Inbox examples include Mews + Opera beside the thread. A logo is not evidence of reservation write-back—confirm path in [Integrations & implementation readiness](#knowledge/integrations). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/independent-hotels)

Agents combine a configurable knowledge base with reservation data; they can check bookings, change reservations, and create tasks only through supported integrations, then pass work the team should handle. How much they resolve “on their own” is explicitly dependent on requests, knowledge, integrations, and rules—not a hotel SLA. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/agents.md)

## Buying committee

Sources do not publish a hotel RACI. What is observable:

- **Independent / boutique:** founder or owner plus lean on-property oversight (Lauderdale: founder; part-time property manager after go-live). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel)
- **Groups:** marketing implies a central brand/knowledge owner and property teams; maintenance use-case copy mentions cluster managers seeing open work—page language, not a named org chart. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/industry/hotel-groups)

Day-to-day users of [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox) are front desk, reservations, and guest services (property or team views, round-robin or custom assignment, human takeover). PMS/IT owners matter for Opera-class connections. Role detail lives in [Buying committee & professional personas](#knowledge/buyer-roles).

## Qualification decisions

Qualify **subsegment → communication job → stack → package → proof**, in that order.

1. Independent hotel vs hotel group vs mis-tagged STR or serviced apartment.
2. Buying locus: one desk and one policy set vs shared standards plus per-property exceptions.
3. Channels: voice and messaging in one workspace; do not assume every OTA thread is live (other catalog pages still mark some OTAs coming soon). [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/product/inbox)
4. Package vs job: Messaging vs Guest (portals, waivers, upsells) vs devices vs Full Suite—see [Pricing & packaging](#knowledge/pricing) and [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities).
5. Proof match: cite Lauderdale only for boutique owner-operator support cost, response time, and modeled asset value, with Conduit attribution and cap-rate caveats. No hotel-group case body is in this pack. Missing group proof means investigate, not reject. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel)

## Signals and next questions

Useful public signals: hotel (not listing) inventory; night phone plus OTA/WhatsApp; PMS names that appear on hotel pages; one GM vs brand standards team. None of these are numeric thresholds.

Ask: Which system is source of truth for reservations, and should guest messaging stay on the PMS? Who owns brand voice versus property exceptions? Which requests must still hit a person at the desk? Is the purchase guest communication, or housekeeping/labor still marked coming soon?

## Disqualifiers and unresolved assumptions

A physical check-in kiosk as the required deliverable is a product mismatch. Operational requirements such as housekeeping or workforce management require feature-level confirmation: navigation says Operations is coming soon while Full Suite lists operational capabilities. That conflict is a readiness question, not an automatic rejection of the hotel account. Separately, transferring STR percentages to hotels or assuming all PMS connectors support the same writes are sales errors, not negative ICP criteria. [Pricing](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing)

Unresolved in sources: no named hotel-group outcomes; Lauderdale’s $600/month and 2-minute average mix AI with a staffed support team, so the human share is not isolated; Portals is a paid add-on by listing count and is not evidenced in the hotel story; implementation effort for hotels is not published here. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel)
open_questions: Is there a named hotel-group customer with documented outcomes, or only industry-page use cases?
For Lauderdale, what mix of AI agents versus 24/7 staffed support produced the $600/month and 2-minute response figures?
Which Opera, Mews, and Cloudbeds actions are live for hotels (read context vs reservation changes, payments, tasks)?
Do independent hotels in practice buy Messaging only or Guest/Portals, given no hotel portal proof in this pack?
Who signs (owner, GM, brand, procurement) when a group wants shared standards plus property exceptions?

choosing independent-hotel vs hotel-group narrative and proof

icp_criteria.criterion: Account operates hotels (independent property or hotel group), not generic contact-center or STR-only inventory
icp_criteria.rationale: Site industries and FAQs name hotel teams separately from short-term rentals; STR proof must not be reused as hotel proof.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Confirm property type from website, PMS (Opera/Mews-class vs STR managers), and whether the desk is a hotel front office.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Investigate operating type before applying hotel or rental ICP; do not reject solely because the label is mixed (e.g. aparthotel).

icp_criteria.criterion: Guest message and/or voice volume that can live in one inbox with property or team views and human handoff
icp_criteria.rationale: Core marketed job is answering calls and messages, acting in connected tools, and escalating with history.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Map current channels (voice, WhatsApp, email, OTA) and who covers the desk after hours.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: If channels are unknown, inventory guest contact paths before packaging; absence of voice is not automatic exclusion if messaging load is real.

icp_criteria.criterion: Reservation/PMS context available to agents (hotel-class systems named on industry pages preferred)
icp_criteria.rationale: Agents and Inbox use property information and booking details; a logo is not a write-action matrix.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Name the PMS, whether messaging stays on the PMS or hotel channels, and which writes are required.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Investigate connector class; do not reject only because the PMS is unlisted—confirm in implementation discovery.

icp_criteria.criterion: Independent vs group model matches workspace needs (single-property policies vs shared brand plus per-property knowledge)
icp_criteria.rationale: Conduit markets distinct independent and group capabilities (shared KB, parent/child, brand voice). Property count is a discovery input, not a published cutoff.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Ask who owns brand standards versus property exceptions and whether conversations should be grouped by property or central team.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: Soft brands, franchises, or mixed portfolios: investigate policy ownership rather than force one subsegment.

icp_criteria.criterion: Primary purchase is guest communication, not a physical check-in kiosk or Operations-as-GA
icp_criteria.rationale: Group page states Conduit is not a physical check-in kiosk; product nav marks Operations coming soon.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Separate hardware check-in, housekeeping/labor systems, and guest messaging in the RFP.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: If the lead is operations-led, investigate timeline and current Agents/Inbox value; do not sell Operations as generally available from these pages.

icp_criteria.criterion: Owner-operator support-cost or hands-off valuation problem similar to Lauderdale
icp_criteria.rationale: The only named hotel story is a boutique owner replacing call-center spend; that pain is not shown as all hotels’ urgency.
icp_criteria.assessment_method: Current third-party support cost, response times, and whether the owner still handles exceptions personally.
icp_criteria.unknown_handling: If this pain is absent, still qualify on after-hours desk load without citing Lauderdale dollar figures.

evidence_validation: Exact passages checked; interpretation and proposed policies require review.

editorial_reviews.reason: Separate genuine product mismatches from readiness questions and seller claim errors.
